description:
Remove the build-provenance feature, its stale-binary guard, and the disk-backed gate TMPDIR it forced.

## Background

Build provenance stamps the git commit, dirty flag, and build timestamp into the binary, reports them from `jit --version`, and backs a stale-binary guard that refuses gate evaluation (exit 10) when the installed binary predates the tree under review. Its contract is proven by three `#[ignore]`d tests in `crates/jit/tests/provenance_contract/`, each of which compiles a whole crate into a fresh temporary target directory.

Measured on this host at `1bd734a2`, that costs more than the feature returns:

- The `provenance` step of a warm `cargo-ci` run measures 116,971 ms of a 192,994 ms total — 61% of the gate.
- Because those tests compile whole crates into `$TMPDIR`, `scripts/cargo-ci.sh:151` moves `TMPDIR` off tmpfs onto a disk-backed cache directory for the entire run. Its comment names the provenance suite as the reason. This repository's tests are filesystem-heavy, so that override taxes every other test in the gate.

The `TMPDIR` cost is the larger of the two, and it was measured directly rather than inferred. Same commit, same warm target, only `TMPDIR` differing:

    TMPDIR on the disk-backed cache dir:  107,493 ms / 104,285 ms
    TMPDIR on tmpfs (/tmp):                18,240 ms /  18,341 ms

That is a 5.8x tax on the whole suite, paid to accommodate three tests.

Recorded gate history agrees, though only correlationally — the suite also grew over the same period. Median `cargo-ci` duration across 1,136 timed runs: 31.7 s (2026-04), 122.0 s (2026-06), 234.8 s (2026-07), 442.1 s (2026-08). Split at the disk-`TMPDIR` commit `c7105be2` (2026-06-18), the median moves 99.7 s to 222.9 s; split at the provenance step `50c57067` (2026-07-15), 120.4 s to 343.4 s.

What the feature buys does not justify that. A stale installed binary was a minor, visible inconvenience before the guard existed; the guard's own remedy is a manual `./scripts/install-jit.sh`. The removal takes the hazard with it: the most expensive guard, `test_metadata_only_change_relinks_no_test_targets`, exists because `build.rs` once declared `.git/index`, `HEAD`, and refs as `rerun-if-changed` inputs, relinking every test target on any `git add` or `git commit`. With `build.rs` reading no git state at all, that regression is unreachable rather than merely guarded.

This blocks `94d85bf1`, which wires the live suite clock into the fixed 30-second checker. Inside `cargo-ci` today that clock reads 69,000-104,000 ms because of the disk `TMPDIR`, so enforcement would fail the gate deterministically on every run however fast the suite itself is. Enforcement is only viable once `TMPDIR` returns to tmpfs.

Removal is a deliberate reduction in shipped surface, not a refactor: `jit --version` loses its provenance fields and exit code 10 ceases to exist. `@/inv/canonical-cutover` governs — remove it cleanly, with no compatibility shim.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The build-provenance feature is removed in full. `crates/jit/build.rs` reads no git state and no clock and stamps no provenance; no `build_provenance`, `BuildProvenance`, or `assess_binary_provenance` symbol remains under `crates/`; `jit --version` in both text and JSON forms reports no commit, dirty, or build-timestamp field.
- [hard] REQ-02: The stale-binary guard is removed. Gate evaluation never refuses on binary age, exit code 10 is no longer emitted or reserved, and its generated reference is regenerated by its own generator rather than hand-edited.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every adopter-facing document describing build provenance, the stale-binary guard, or exit code 10 is updated to match the shipped surface, including all four sites in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md`. `jit validate` exits 0 and every document reference resolves.
- [hard] REQ-04: The `provenance_contract` test suite is deleted, along with any helper it alone used. No property that another suite does not already cover is silently dropped: any assertion worth keeping is identified explicitly and relocated, and anything deleted outright is named with the reason it no longer applies.
- [hard] REQ-05: `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` runs no provenance step and sets no `TMPDIR` override, so the gate inherits the host default. Its comment explaining the override is removed with it, and `scripts/install-jit.sh` no longer embeds a dirty flag.
- [hard] REQ-06: A warm `cargo-ci` run on this host records a `suite-clock` at or below 25,000 ms and a total gate duration at or below 45,000 ms, measured from an already-built target, with the per-step evidence retained.
- [hard] REQ-07: The full workspace suite passes, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports zero warnings.
- [hard] REQ-08: The removal is clean. No vestigial symbol, module, config key, script flag, environment variable, test helper, fixture, generated-document region, or prose reference to build provenance, the stale-binary guard, or exit code 10 survives outside `dev/archive/` and historical benchmark artifacts, which are records of what was and stay untouched. The issues that introduced this feature are read for context and their additions withdrawn in full: `2b82c12c` (local CLI version provenance), `129f3fad` (scoping the guard to build-input changes), `5d862134`, `32779829`, and `83efbcb4`. A surviving fragment is a defect of this task, not a follow-up.

## Notes

Trace the footprint before editing: `git grep -ln "build_provenance\|BuildProvenance\|assess_binary_provenance"` reports 71 files, most of them archived documents and benchmark artifacts that must be left alone. The live code is `crates/jit/src/domain/build_provenance.rs`, `domain/repository_inputs.rs`, `domain/binary_build_inputs.txt`, `domain/mod.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `gate_execution.rs`, `errors.rs`, and `main.rs`, plus `build.rs`, `scripts/install-jit.sh`, and `scripts/install-jit-selftest.sh`.

Issues `2b82c12c`, `129f3fad`, `5d862134`, `32779829`, and `83efbcb4` built this feature; their work is being withdrawn deliberately, not by accident. Read each with `jit issue show <id>` before editing — together they are the inventory of what was added, and they are the cheapest way to find a fragment that a grep for the obvious symbol names would miss.

Do not weaken the removal into a feature flag or an opt-out. The point is that the code, its tests, and the `TMPDIR` override all leave together.
title: Remove build provenance, the stale-binary guard, and the disk-backed gate TMPDIR
